limitations: Recommended customer prices are current advertised Intel guidance, not realized net prices or prices available to every buyer. This is not a historical launch-price series.
Selected high-core pairs illustrate content change. They do not represent sales-weighted product mix, replacement rates or actual average selling prices.
Cores are not interchangeable across generations or workload types. No throughput, latency, power consumed, system TCO or price-performance claim follows from core count or TDP alone.
Package footprint is not actual wafer area, yield, substrate-layer demand, cost or the limiting manufacturing resource. It indicates physical change only.

owned_model_requirement.formula: Completed-work capacity = package units * workload throughput per package. CPU revenue per unit of completed-work capacity = realized package ASP / workload throughput per package.
owned_model_requirement.interpretation: Richer packages can raise Intel revenue per package while lowering the customer's CPU expenditure per workload. That can support adoption, but a package-volume forecast additionally needs sufficiently expanding workload demand, replacement demand or share gains. The illustrative throughput gains are not measured Intel forecasts.

share_volume_identity.formula: Intel package units = addressable package market units * Intel unit share. Required market growth = 1.20 / (1 + relative Intel share change) - 1.
share_volume_identity.limitation: Do not substitute hyperscaler Arm share, server-system shipment share, x86 revenue share or core share into a CPU-package unit-share identity. No particular market growth or future Intel share is forecast here.
